chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all together, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The kiss does not break the fast.
ai.seo_question: Does kissing break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* through the chain of Jamil and Zurarah, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that simple kissing does not break the fast, a ruling that distinguishes it from acts causing ejaculation or sexual intercourse. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for defining the boundaries of *mu'asharah* (foreplay), emphasizing that minor intimacy without emission or swallowing does not nullify the fast, thereby encouraging believers to maintain closeness during Ramadan without fear of invalidating their worship.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, altogether, rom Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The kissing does not break the Fast’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from and Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Kissing does not destroy the fast.’”
